items.stem: If a family farm produces corn and uses part of it for consumption, what is the primary purpose of the remaining corn?

What is the main reason economies have to make choices?

What does a point below the production possibility frontier represent according to the passage?
If an economy decides to produce more investment goods, what is the likely effect on future consumption?
What is the main purpose of the production possibility frontier in the passage?

In a society, if people want more corn than what is produced, what is the likely economic consequence?

Which of the following is a branch of economics that studies the behaviour of individual economic agents?
What are the physical, tangible objects used to satisfy people's wants and needs called?
What is the term for a decision-making unit that can be a single person or a group?
